newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Power sees 317 mln stg windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Power sees 317 mln stg windfall tax.

text.p: British multi-utility Scottish Power Plc said on Wednesday it estimated it was liable to pay some 317 million stg as its part of the UK 'windfall levy'.
Chairman Murray Stuart also told the annual general meeting that trading activities in the first three months of the current financial year were in line with its expectations.
The windfall levy will be payable in two instalments, the first of which is due in December this year.
"Your board is still considering the impact of this levy upon the company's business plans and future strategy," Stuart said in a statement.
Scottish Power, whose activities span electricity, water, gas, telecoms and electrical retailing, is one of the largest utility businesses in the UK, serving one in five UK homes.

As well as making further progress towards the complete deregulation of the electricity and gas markets in 1998, it aims to capture by year 2000 some 15 percent of the UK electricity market and 12 percent of the gas market in the three regions in which it competes.
Scottish Telecom aims to secure 10 percent of the Scottish market by year 2000, a market it says is forecast to be valued at 2.0 billion by then.

The acquisitions of Manweb and Southern Water were "both delivering further operational and financial progress resulting in an enhancement to shareholder value which is ahead of our original expectations," Stuart added.
